description: Integrative capstone tracing a representative female northern elephant seal over a full annual cycle, linking oxygen stores, diving, foraging energetics, buoyancy feedback, EEG-measured sleep, water conservation, molting endocrinology, delayed implantation, lactation and lifetime breeding success. Distinguishes direct sensor readings from modeled inferences.

related_resources.reason: Marked-female life tables at Año Nuevo, seasonality, delayed implantation, pup development, lifetime reproduction.
Long-term individual breeding and life-history study; NPS account gives accessible overview.
Time-depth and tracking records, two foraging trips, methods and measurement limitations.
Blood volume, myoglobin, condition and dive duration in females; abstract publicly available.
Measurements under controlled voluntary dives and caution against direct extrapolation to field energetics.
Cardiovascular diving response, gas exchange, tissue oxygen delivery and variability across dives.
Field metabolic rates, flipper strokes, drag comparison, condition and reproductive allocation.
Drift-rate and stroke logger data show shifts in buoyancy and efficient locomotion as seals gain fat.
Prey-capture proxies and energy deficits in one female; limitations of interpreting foraging activity.
EEG, accelerometry and dive behavior, short sleep bouts and extrapolated at-sea sleep duration.
Milk lipid/energy output and maternal fasting physiology with underlying source citations.
Experiments on respiratory evaporative water loss in fasting pups, with apnea and nasal structures.
Water turnover, metabolic water production and long fasting in weaned pups.
Protein sparing, changing protein contribution and renal function late in maternal lactation.
ACTH intervention with cortisol, aldosterone, thyroid and immune measurements at two molting stages.
Species-specific overview of timing, embryonic diapause, and association with seasonal cycle.
Seasonal movements and routes, contrasts between male and female migration.
